verses.text: Now, about the questions you wrote to me: it is good for a man to abstain from sexual relations with a woman.
But because sexual immorality is a danger, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.
A husband should give his wife the affection he owes her, and a wife should do the same for her husband.

A wife does not have authority over her own body by herself; her husband shares that authority. In the same way, a husband does not have authority over his own body by himself; his wife shares that authority.
Do not deprive each other, unless you both agree to pause for a time so you can devote yourselves to prayer. Then come together again, so Satan will not tempt you because self-control is difficult.
I’m saying this as a concession, not as a command.
I wish everyone could be as I am, but each person has their own gift from God—one has this gift, another has a different one.
I say to those who are unmarried and to widows: it is good for them to remain as I am.
But if they cannot control their desires, they should marry. It is better to marry than to be consumed by passion.
To those who are married, I give this command—not from me, but from the Lord: a wife must not leave her husband.
If she does leave, she must remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not leave his wife.
To the others, I say this—I, not the Lord: if a believer has an unbelieving wife who is willing to live with him, he must not leave her.
And if a woman has an unbelieving husband who is willing to live with her, she must not leave him.

For the unbelieving husband is set apart through his believing wife, and the unbelieving wife is set apart through her believing husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
But if the unbelieving partner leaves, let them go. In that situation, the brother or sister is not bound. God has called you to live in peace.
Wife, how can you know whether you will save your husband? Husband, how can you know whether you will save your wife?
Each person should live in the way the Lord assigned and God called them to. This is the rule I give in all the churches.
Was someone circumcised when God called him? He should not try to undo it. Was someone uncircumcised when called? He should not be circumcised.
Circumcision means nothing, and being uncircumcised means nothing. What matters is keeping God’s commands.
Each person should remain in the situation they were in when God called them.
Were you enslaved when you were called? Do not let it trouble you. But if you can gain your freedom, take that opportunity.
A person enslaved when called by the Lord is the Lord’s free person. In the same way, a free person called by the Lord is Christ’s servant.
You were bought at a price. Do not become enslaved to people.
Brothers and sisters, each of you should remain with God in the situation you were in when called.
About those who have never married: I have no command from the Lord, but I’ll give my judgment as someone the Lord has shown mercy to and made trustworthy.
I think that, because of the present distress, it is good for a person to remain as they are.
Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you free from a wife? Do not seek one.
But if you marry, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Still, those who marry will face trouble in this life, and I want to spare you that.
Brothers and sisters, I mean this: the time is short. From now on, those who have wives should live as if they did not;
those who grieve as if they were not grieving, those who celebrate as if they were not celebrating, and those who buy as if they owned nothing;
and those who use the things of this world as if they were not using them fully. For the present form of this world is passing away.
I want you to be free from anxiety. An unmarried man is concerned about the Lord’s work and how to please the Lord.
But a married man is concerned about the things of this world and how to please his wife.

There is also a difference between a wife and a virgin. An unmarried woman is concerned about the Lord’s work, so she can be holy in body and spirit. But a married woman is concerned about the things of this world and how to please her husband.
I’m saying this for your benefit, not to trap you. I want you to live in a fitting way and stay devoted to the Lord without distraction.
But if a man thinks he is behaving improperly toward his virgin, if she is past the usual age for marriage, and if it should be so, he should do what he wishes. He is not sinning; let them marry.
But the man who stands firm in his heart, feels no pressure, controls his own will, and has decided in his heart to keep his own virgin unmarried does well.
So the man who gives his own virgin in marriage does well, and the one who does not give her in marriage does better.
A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, as long as it is in the Lord.
In my judgment, she would be happier if she stayed as she is. And I think I, too, have God’s Spirit.
